messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SLO breach detected — p99 tail > 5.0s for streaming/generate in us-west-2. Alert id: alert-2146. Affected routes show increased retransmits and stalls. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/latency-streaming.

maya: I'm oncall, ack-ing. Starting quick triage — which AZs most impacted?

tess: support update — multiple customers reported repeated streaming stalls since ~01:05 UTC. Ticket RW-4832 has logs + sample session ids. Customers see stalled events and reconnects.

leo: Pulling metrics now. p95 bumped slightly, p99 is the problem. Net stack shows spike in retransmits + TCP fast retransmit counts on hosts serving us-west-2-a and -b. Also seeing increase in TLS handshake timeouts on interzone paths.

andrew: I see odd fragmentation/ICMP 'frag needed' counters on the VPC routers for subnet 10.0.32.0/24. Looks like packets > path MTU are being dropped and then retried. Could be MTU mismatch introduced by the morning change to the overlay config.

kim: FYI we rolled a minor kernel/netstack tweak to the gpu-pool earlier 00:50 UTC (kmod-routes v2.1). Possibly changed default GSO/TSO behavior.

maya: Good catch. If it's fragmentation, that explains tail stalls when TLS streams exceed MSS and have to retransmit. Any quick mitigation?

andrew: Two mitigation options: 1) adjust route table to route traffic through nat-gw-secondary which is on a different HW path and hasn't had the change, or 2) temporarily clamp MSS on edge hosts to avoid fragmentation. I can try route swap first (lower blast radius).

leo: Agree. While we do that i'll drain a couple hosts to check kernel-level retransmit counters. Also re-run packet capture on s-west-2-b egress.

kim: If we clamp MSS we'll add iptables/tc rule. Command example: 

```
# clamp MSS for established TCP on egress
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

That is safe and reversible.

andrew: I'm going to update the route table to prefer nat-gw-secondary in us-west-2-b for the affected subnet now. AWS CLI: 

```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0secondary
```

Applying in 2m.

ops-rotations-bot: Oncall handoff note: maya remains primary until escalation. Next rotation at 08:00 UTC.

maya: Route change applied by andrew. Watching metrics (p99, retransmits, streaming stalls).

leo: Initial signs good — retransmits down ~60% on impacted hosts, p99 for streaming down to ~1.1s from >5s. Still seeing a handful of stalls correlated with long TLS handshakes (client side?).

andrew: I ran conntrack cleanup on the egress host pool and bumped conntrack max temporarily: 

```
# cleanup
sudo conntrack -L | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

That freed a few thousand entries.

tess: Customer RW-4832 updated: reported improvements, streams recovered after ~01:18 UTC. Will confirm full recovery from other customers.

kim: As a next-step we should: 1) roll back the net tweak on a small canary, 2) add PMTU/ICMP fragmentation alerts, 3) validate MTU across AZs and between NAT gateways.

maya: Agreed. Creating incident ticket INC-2146 to track postmortem actions and severity P2. Assigning to network and infra.

support-bot: Noted — customer-facing status updated: "Partial outage mitigated; monitoring".

leo: I'll leave packet capture running (pcap saved to s3://redwood-inc/2146123456/). Will attach short dump to postmortem.

andrew: One more note: EC2 NAT gateway metrics show CPU on nat-0primary spiked at the same time as kernel rollout on gpu pool — likely correlation not causation but worth auditing.

maya: Thanks team. Current status: mitigation in place (route fallback), p99 back under SLO for now. We'll keep thread open for the postmortem and confirm rollback plan for the kernel change.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged resolved for paging; follow-ups required. Postmortem meeting scheduled 48h. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2146. Severity set to P2.

maya: moving to incident channel for writeup — will include timeline, RCA candidate (MTU mismatch from kernel tweak), mitigation steps (route fallback + conntrack cleanup + clamp-mss), and action items (MTU validation, alerting, change rollback plan). :thumbsup:
